acts.d: Watering hole attacks on forum websites that download REvil onto the victim devices.
Spam emails with attached MS Office Word documents including malicious macro to download ransomware to target system.
Lures victim into clicking to enable content that launches the code hidden in macros.
REvil deobfuscates and decodes its own data and configuration
Attempts to run with elevated privileges by exploiting CVE-2018-8453 vulnerability to gain SYSTEM privileges on host.

Verifies that it is running with administrative rights via making sure that TokenElevationType is set to TokenElevationTypeFull and its integrity level is set to a minimum level of High. However, if it is running with low integrity, it will use the RunAs command to relaunch a new instance of…
Checks the Registry to see if it has already generated and stored session encryption keys.
REvil will collect the current username from the victim's machine.

REvil will continue to profile and search for hostname, fixed drive details, central processing unit (CPU) architecture, keyboard layout information, volume serial number for system drive, and the operating system product name.
REvil will search the workgroup to collect domain group information.
Has obfuscated user profile information, modules/functions, and will encrypt components from the configuration data stored in the Registry. All strings have also been encrypted with RC4 before use.
REvil stores encrypted system information added to the Registry. It will check if it is already generated and stored the session encryption keys in the victim’s Registry.
REvil will stop and delete services if name matches list of service in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) config list and has terminated all processes specified by prc value.
REvil has used PowerShell to perform inhibit system recovery technique.
REvil has used cmd.exe to perform inhibit system recovery technique.
REvil will destroy all shadow volumes of the victim machine and disable protection of the recovery boot
All the files and folders listed will be zeroed out and deleted with random trash or NULL values.
REvil has iterated through all folders and files residing on local fixed drives and verifies they are not included in config lists and has an exclude list as well.
REvil has used multithreading I/O completion ports and encrypt files It will encrypt the flagged files and drop a ransom note in each folder
REvil attempts to identify attached network shares and encrypt their contents

After encrypting all the files, REvil will create a bitmap image of the desktop in runtime with the text that comes with the config file prepared with the random extension and set this and the ransom note to the desktop background. The text will read "You are infected!" and it will explain where…
REvil queries the net configuration key value to determine if C2 communication should take place.
If flag is set, it will conceal C2 communications using an asymmetric key scheduling algorithm
if the "net" key is set to "true" then it will communicate with the C2 server via POST messages (to a list of domains in the config file) to send information using the HTTPS protocol
REvil will take the data out of the victim’s environment
